body_es: Waterfall es un enfoque secuencial donde cada fase (requisitos, diseño, implementación, pruebas, despliegue) debe completarse antes de comenzar la siguiente, lo que resulta en largas duraciones de proyecto y dificultades para incorporar cambios posteriores. Agile, por el contrario, organiza el trabajo en iteraciones cortas donde el software funcional se entrega regularmente, permitiendo feedback temprano y adaptación continua. Mientras Waterfall es predecible pero inflexible, Agile es adaptable pero requiere mayor comunicación y disciplina en el equipo para mantener el ritmo iterativo.
body_en: Waterfall is a sequential approach where each phase (requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment) must be completed before the next begins, resulting in long project durations and difficulty incorporating later changes. Agile, conversely, organizes work into short iterations where functional software is delivered regularly, enabling early feedback and continuous adaptation. While Waterfall is predictable but inflexible, Agile is adaptable but requires greater team communication and discipline to maintain iterative pace.
example_code:
# Comparison: Waterfall vs Agile Timeline
waterfall:
  requirements: "Months 1-2"
  design: "Months 3-4"
  implementation: "Months 5-8"
  testing: "Months 9-10"
  deployment: "Month 11"
  total_duration: "11 months"
  feedback_point: "End of project"

agile:
  sprint_1: "Weeks 1-2: Complete feature, test, deploy"
  sprint_2: "Weeks 3-4: Next feature, test, deploy"
  sprint_3: "Weeks 5-6: Continue iterations"
  feedback_point: "After each sprint (2 weeks)"
  adaptation: "Changes incorporated quickly"
example_output:
Waterfall:
- Timeline: 11 months
- Feedback: End of cycle
- Changes: Expensive and difficult

Agile:
- Timeline: Continuous delivery every 2 weeks
- Feedback: Immediate after each sprint
- Changes: Expected and welcomed
